ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure on the right, a light rod OA of length l has its O end fixed with a hinge, and a small ball A is fixed at the other end; the light rod leans against an object of height h. If the friction between the object and the ground is neglected, then when the object moves rightward with speed v until the angle between the rod and the horizontal direction is θ, the contact point between the object and the light rod is B. Which of the following statements is correct?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The angular velocity of rotation of the light rod is $\frac{v\sin^{2}\theta}h$

If the friction between the object and the ground is neglected, then when the object moves rightward with speed v until the angle between the rod and the horizontal direction is θ, find the angular velocity of rotation of the light rod.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the lower left of the figure there is hinge point O. The light rod OA extends obliquely upward to the right from O, and near the end of the rod is labeled A; the angle between the rod and the horizontal ground is labeled θ. On the right side there is a rectangular object. The light rod contacts the upper edge of the object, and the contact point is labeled B; on the right side of the object there is a rightward arrow, indicating that the object moves rightward with speed v. The problem text gives the height of the object as h. Reasoning: The contact point B is located at the top end of the object, so the vertical coordinate of point B equals the height h of the object. Also because B is on the light rod, and the light rod makes an angle θ with the horizontal, in the right triangle from O to B there is OB·sinθ=h, that is, OB=h/sinθ. The horizontal coordinate of point B is x_B=OB·cosθ=(h/sinθ)cosθ=h cotθ. When the object moves rightward, the horizontal position of its contact with the rod changes rightward with speed v along with the object, so dx_B/dt=v. Differentiate x_B=h cotθ with respect to time: dx_B/dt=-h csc²θ·dθ/dt. Taking the magnitude of the angular velocity, there is v=h csc²θ·ω, therefore ω=v sin²θ/h.
